answer: Hardware-attested keys bind each agent to a physical secure chip: its signing key lives in a TPM whose maker certificate peers verify, and each chip may register only one identity. Faking N heads means buying N real devices, so cost climbs with every head. A periodic pulse of signed challenges checks the chip stays online, and a chip shared or cloned is struck off; past that horizon, a farm of virtual heads is as hollow as a painted marble.
